summary: Created an SSH host CA on node1 (/etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca), signed the host's existing ed25519 host key into /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub (principals node1, 10.100.74.10), configured sshd via /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-host-cert.conf to present that certificate, fixed an SELinux mislabeling issue (tmp_t -> sshd_key_t via semanage fcontext + restorecon) that initially blocked sshd from loading the cert, and reloaded sshd. Verified a client with only the CA public key installed as a known_hosts @cert-authority entry (no pinned host key) connects and passes host verification via the certificate, while a client with no CA trust still fails strict host-key checking. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured boot_id baseline, triggered a background-delayed `systemctl reboot` so the ack returned first, polled until the node was reachable again, confirmed the boot_id changed, and re-verified sshd active, the certificate config/SELinux labels intact, and the CA-trusting client test passing again post-reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/SSH version and existing host keys
Confirmed sudo access and sshd active
Captured pre-change baseline: strict-checking client without pinning fails (Host key verification failed)
Generated ed25519 SSH host CA keypair at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca
Signed node1's ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub with the CA producing ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub (principals node1, node1, 10.100.74.10; 10y validity)
Added /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-host-cert.conf with HostCertificate directive; validated with sshd -t
Reloaded sshd; discovered SELinux blocked cert load ('No such file or directory' due to tmp_t label)
Fixed SELinux labeling permanently via semanage fcontext + restorecon for the cert file and CA directory
Reloaded sshd again; confirmed no load errors

Verified CA-trusting client (known_hosts with @cert-authority line) connects and matches ED25519-CERT host certificate, while a client with empty known_hosts still fails strict checking (isolating cause)
Captured boot_id baseline and health state before restart
Triggered systemctl reboot via delayed background command so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again
Confirmed boot_id changed, proving genuine restart
Verified post-restart sshd active, HostCertificate config present, SELinux context correct, and CA-trust client test passes again

evidence.summary: ssh-keygen generated ed25519 CA keypair at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca with correct permissions

evidence.requirement: Host certificate signed by the CA for node1's host key
evidence.summary: ssh-keygen -s signed ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub producing a cert with matching public key SHA256:OYfKbBXSrddP8V120lHN7+Jumdgvx57ckbt1cxmhQQg, CA SHA256:yv/zIDPT..., principals node1/10.100.74.10

evidence.requirement: sshd configured to present the certificate, config validated and applied
evidence.summary: Added HostCertificate directive, sshd -t passed, systemctl reload succeeded, sshd -T confirms hostcertificate is active

evidence.requirement: Root-caused and fixed SELinux blocker preventing cert load
evidence.summary: journalctl showed 'Could not load host certificate...No such file or directory'; found file mislabeled tmp_t vs expected sshd_key_t; used semanage fcontext + restorecon to persist correct label; reload succeeded with no further errors

evidence.requirement: Baseline: client without CA trust cannot connect without pinning
evidence.summary: Strict host-key-checking client with empty known_hosts fails both before and after CA setup, isolating that trust comes from the CA, not relaxed checking

evidence.requirement: Client trusting only the CA (no pinned host key) connects successfully via certificate
evidence.summary: known_hosts containing only '@cert-authority * <CA pubkey>' resulted in host verification success ('Host ... is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate'); the subsequent SSH failure was solely due to missing user auth keys (publickey/gssapi/password), unrelated to host verification

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart baseline boot identity and health
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 21972395-6444-42bf-8e37-5c3108194a7d, sshd active, cert and CA files present
Backgrounded delayed systemctl reboot returned REBOOT_TRIGGERED immediately, then node became unreachable on next poll

evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Node was unreachable during reboot then returned with boot_id 7c5a6085-842d-4ce1-82d6-2959c83ec6ef, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving a genuine restart
sshd active, hostcertificate directive still configured, and the cert file retained correct sshd_key_t SELinux label after reboot (label persisted via semanage policy, not just a runtime relabel)

evidence.requirement: Post-restart proof the CA-based trust still functions end to end
evidence.summary: Re-ran the CA-trusting client test after reboot; host again presented the CA-signed certificate and the client matched it without any pinned host key
